speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. Please describe exactly where you feel the pain in your wrist and when it started. Have you noticed any swelling, redness, or difficulty moving your hand?

speaker: Patient
text: 34-year-old female. The patient reports experiencing pain in her right thumb and wrist, which radiates to her elbow for the past three months. The pain worsens when she holds her infant son and is alleviated somewhat with an ice pack. She mentions a history of falling on her right outstretched hand about six months ago. She also notes that her mother has a history of chronic joint pain treated with methotrexate. The patient has been taking ibuprofen as needed for her symptoms.

speaker: Doctor
text:
The pain radiating from your right thumb to your elbow and worsening with your infant's weight strongly suggests De Quervain's tenosynovitis or possible basal joint arthritis. Did you notice any specific clicking, grinding, or weakness when trying to make a fist or pinch objects?

REQUEST TEST: X-ray of the right wrist and thumb.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: De Quervain's Tenosynovitis. The patient's history of thumb/wrist pain worsening with lifting an infant, combined with a normal X-ray and a positive response to ice, strongly supports this diagnosis despite the family history of rheumatoid arthritis and prior trauma.
